_about: Rules, regulations and notifications made under the Companies Act, 2017, with the sections they carry out. `library` names the instrument's id when its text is in the library; `sections` lists the Act's sections; `basis` says where the link comes from; `confirm` lists what still has to be checked against the instrument itself. Sections cited by instruments in the library are found automatically and need not be listed here. `url` links to the instrument's page on the regulator's website; `found` records how the details were found (`search-index`: from a web search engine's index of the regulator's site, to be confirmed against the instrument). `madeUnder` names the other law under which an instrument was made, for instruments not made under this Act that do what a section leaves to be specified (shown as “Other law”). `setInOrder` lists sections whose details are fixed in each order or notice, so no rule or regulation is expected (shown as “Set in each order”, not “To identify”).

instruments.title: Companies (Court) Rules, 1997
instruments.basis: Made by the Federal Government on the advice of the Supreme Court, in consultation with the High Courts, under section 438 of the Companies Ordinance, 1984 (recital). Section 423 of this Act is the corresponding rule-making power for proceedings before the Court; no rules under section 423 have been found. They also contain what sections 317, 320 and 339 leave to be prescribed: limits of the official liquidator's remuneration (rule 256), the statement of affairs and its form (rules 104–106), and the official liquidator's accounts, their forms and audit (rules 259–264, Forms 101–103). These rules refer to the sections of the 1984 Ordinance (for example section 328 for the statement of affairs) and require quarterly accounts, whereas section 339 provides for half-yearly accounts. For voluntary winding up they give forms for the declaration of solvency (rule 269, Form 107; 1984 section 362, now section 351), the statement of assets and liabilities laid before creditors (rule 270, Form 108; 1984 section 368, now section 357), the notice of the final meeting and the account laid before it (rule 279, Forms 111 and 112) and the returns to the registrar after it (rule 281, Forms 113 and 114; 1984 sections 370 and 382, now sections 359 and 369), and the liquidator's periodical statements of pending liquidations (rule 267, Forms 104–106; 1984 section 430, now section 415). Rules 252–254 deal with moneys of a company in liquidation paid into the bank (section 416). Sections 351, 357, 359 and 369 leave these particulars to be specified by regulations, which have not been found; the rules are the nearest existing provision. All 115 forms of the rules are matched by subject to sections of this Act on a separate page; the compromise forms (19–21) have no counterpart because the Commission, not the Court, now sanctions compromises (sections 279 and 280). Sections 315, 337 and 341 are not linked here although forms touch them, because what they leave to be specified or prescribed (the panel of liquidators, persons to assist the official liquidator, transfer of a section 42 company's assets) is not in the rules. Section 423 of this Act is the power under which rules of this kind are now to be made; no rules made under it have been found.
